details:
SpectraShiftX is an AI-powered astronomical analysis platform developed as part of our NASA Space Apps Challenge project, Echoes of the Sky. It uses data from NASA's SPHEREx space telescope to explore the universe, detect unusual spectral patterns, and identify potentially interesting astronomical objects.

The platform works by analyzing astronomical FITS data using Python and scientific libraries. It processes celestial coordinates, examines spectral information, detects unusual variations, and applies machine learning techniques to identify anomalies that might deserve further investigation. The results are presented through an interactive web interface, making complex scientific data easier to explore and understand.

Our project offers several benefits. It simplifies the exploration of large astronomical datasets, helps highlight unusual cosmic phenomena, and makes scientific information more accessible to students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts. Its intended impact is to support astronomical research by providing an accessible way to explore data and identify potential discoveries that might otherwise be overlooked.

To develop SpectraShiftX, we used Python for scientific data processing and analysis. We also used React and Vite for the frontend, FastAPI for backend communication.

Throughout development, our team considered scientific accuracy, data accessibility, computational limitations, user experience, and the need to make complex astronomical concepts understandable. We also focused on building a functional minimum viable product without requiring users to download or process massive astronomical datasets themselves.
